cards.title: Introduction to Migrations
cards.content: EF Core Migrations provide a way to incrementally update the database schema to match your application's data model changes while preserving existing data in the database.

items.text: Modify the C# entity classes or DbContext
Run 'dotnet ef migrations add <Name>' in the terminal
Review the generated migration code for accuracy
Run 'dotnet ef database update' to apply changes

cards.title: Anatomy of a Migration
cards.content:
A migration file consists of two primary methods:

  • Up(): Applies the changes to move the database forward to the new state.
  • Down(): Reverts the changes to return the database to the previous state.
protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
{
    migrationBuilder.AddColumn<string>(
        name: "Email",
        table: "Users",
        nullable: true);
}

cards.title: Complete the Command
cards.content: To generate a new migration file with a specific name in EF Core, you use the command: dotnet ef migrations ________ <MigrationName>

cards.title: Match EF Core Commands to Actions

pairs.right: Creates a new migration skeleton based on model changes
Applies pending migrations to the database
Deletes the last migration if it hasn't been applied
Generates a SQL script from migrations

cards.title: Migrations in Production
cards.content:
When deploying to production, running database update automatically might not be ideal due to permission restrictions or lack of rollback control.

Best practices include:

  • Generating SQL scripts using dotnet ef migrations script.
  • Reviewing the SQL scripts with DBAs before execution.
  • Applying scripts manually during release pipelines.
